report_text: The eight slides for Topic 19 provide a clear, self‑contained explanation of DevOps.  The definition is stated twice – first as a set of practices that combine development and operations, and again as a set of practices that automate the processes between the two teams to enable faster, more reliable software delivery.  The slides explicitly state that DevOps “aims to shorten the system development life cycle (SDLC)” and to improve an organization’s ability to deliver and support applications.  Finally, the historical conflict between development and operations is addressed in a dedicated section: developers prioritize rapid feature delivery and low lead time, while operations prioritize stability, uptime, and cost‑efficiency.  The differing metrics and incentives are highlighted, explaining why the two groups have traditionally had conflicting goals.  All three student questions are answered within the topic’s slide range, so the deck does not exhibit a gap for this topic.
